status: Eight lead-approved null-to-image replacements integrated, eight held and excluded. Episode count unchanged; RSS delta +2. No publication.

entries.title: I said that
entries.body: I introduced myself to a passing fish. It said hello to the branch above me. I corrected it. It tried the branch below. By the time it found my face, I wasn't feeling very welcoming.

image.title: File:Pygmy Seahorse - Hippocampus bargibanti.jpg
image.creator: Steve Childs
image.description: A Pygmy Seahorse (Hippocampus bargibanti)
image.sceneMatch: The seahorse's face and body nearly merge with the red-knobbed coral. Mistakenly addressing branches is fictional dialogue grounded in the actual concealment.

entries.status: Lead held: branch introductions repeat Vera.

entries.title: A little too secure
entries.body: I told him I was relaxed. He glanced at my tail. I loosened it one turn. The branch moved. I put the turn back before either of us could form an opinion.

image.title: File:Pygmy Seahorse (Hippocampus bargibanti) (6079487627).jpg
image.creator: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE
image.description: Nudi Retreat II, Lembeh Strait, Sulawesi, INDONESIA
image.sceneMatch: Tail is visibly wound tightly around a coral branch. The claim of relaxation is contradicted by that exact bodily grip.

entries.status: Lead approved exact prose and image; integrated at the specified stable runtime slot.

entries.title: You first
entries.body:
He asked me to let go of the branch for a moment. He would stay beside me.

I asked why.

He said there wasn't a reason. We could just float a little.

I unwound my tail halfway. Then I thought of a reason to keep the rest wrapped. Then several.

He waited. I asked whether he was still holding on.

Very tightly, he said.

We stayed like that for a while, each considering the other's excellent support.

Eventually I suggested we begin by being slightly less attached to the idea.

entries.title: The full distance
entries.body: A fish asked how far away the other side of the fan was. I told her it depended how many places she intended to panic. She said she meant in a straight line. I don't know anyone who lives like that.

image.sceneMatch: Close seahorse face among dense forked coral branches supports a small resident's grip-by-grip account of distance. No actual travel distance is asserted.

entries.status: Lead approved exact prose and image; integrated at the specified stable runtime slot.

entries.title: Still arriving
entries.body: I meant to make a brief appearance. Someone said it was nice to see all of me. I had not realised how much of me had joined in.

image.title: File:Anguila listón azul (Rhinomuraena quaesita), Anilao, Filipinas, 2023-08-23, DD 59.jpg
image.creator: Diego Delso
image.sceneMatch: Long blue eel body extends well beyond its shelter across the image. The surprise concerns the substantial visible length, not a move between burrows.

entries.title: Before the blue
entries.body:
When I was black, I thought the blue ones knew where they were going. They came out of the reef so slowly that it looked as though the water had been waiting for them.

I tried swimming like that. I was still small enough for the current to have a different idea. Half of me went where I intended. The other half described what I thought of it.

I am blue now. Yesterday a young eel watched me emerge.

I took my time.

There was a small bit of me caught on something behind the rock. I have no intention of telling him.

entries.title: Much better for the current
entries.body: I said I needed more space. He withdrew. A little too far, I thought. I told him the current felt different now. He came back up. I said that was much better for the current.

entries.title: She knew already
entries.body: She recognised me before I came out. I had been blue for a week and was hoping for a much more complicated reunion.

image.title: File:Rhinomuraena quaesita 64219021.jpg

entries.title: Still shaking
entries.body: I tried to shake a bit of weed off. Everything shook. I stopped to see which bit was the weed. Everything stopped. This could take the rest of my life.

entries.title: The last millimetre
entries.body: A shrimp landed on my snout. I bent toward it. So did my snout. I tried from the other side. We went round together. Eventually lunch got bored with me and left.

image.caption: 0:9 File:Phycodurus eques P2023167.JPG
image.sceneMatch: The close side portrait clearly shows the rigid projecting snout. The temporary shrimp visitor is offscreen fiction; do not claim the photograph documents a shrimp.

entries.title: Something in my eye
entries.body:
A frill kept passing in front of my eye. My own frill. I would wait for a clear view, start toward the grass, and lose the grass again.

He found me turning in little circles. I told him I was looking for a route.

He stayed on the side where I could see. When the frill covered him, he moved a little farther out. I followed his snout through the tangle.

It was such a small thing to notice about someone. I wanted to tell him that.

I opened my mouth and sucked in a shrimp between us.

He waited. I swallowed. By then it seemed best to keep following.

image.caption: 0:11 File:Phycodurus eques P2023182.JPG

entries.status: Lead held: actual photograph does not establish own frill obstructing vision.

entries.title: One more place
entries.body: Somewhere between the grass and the rock, I lost a piece of weed that had been caught in my frills. I went back to look for it. I know. I spent the whole morning trying to get it off.

image.title: File:Phycodurus eques P2023181.JPG

image.description: Leafy sea dragon Phycodurus eques at Rapid Bay Jetty, Gulf St Vincent, South Australia
image.caption: 0:12 File:Phycodurus eques P2023181.JPG
image.sceneMatch: Whole animal among branching vegetation supports a small caught weed, not a photographed loss. Intentionally ambivalent attachment to an irritant; no house or habitat move.

entries.status: Lead held: weak nostalgia for weed.

entries.title: A decent scratch
entries.body:
The rough bit fitted just behind my fin. I leaned into it and nearly stopped swimming altogether.

I went past again. Slower. There was one point where I could get the itch exactly, but only if I stuck my face into the weed and lifted my tail.

I had been doing this for some time when a little fish came round the corner. I straightened so fast I lost the spot.

It waited. I waited. It nibbled something. I tried to look like a fish with somewhere else to go.

Then the itch started again.

I put my face back in the weed. The little fish could tell whoever it wanted.

entries.title: The one underneath
entries.body: My shadow got thin as I rose off the sand. Came down: fat again. Up. Down. I did this until I was tired, then rested on the sand looking exactly the way I had been trying not to.

entries.title: A smaller target
entries.body: I turned sideways to let the current past. It found the other side. Tried facing it. Mouthful of water. I am running out of arrangements of fish.

entries.title: Don't get up
entries.body: I settled on the sand beside her. Very comfortable. She moved a little. I moved a little. She moved again. I followed. We are resting quite a long way from where we started.
